note: Recast from the description of the new species by Rocha & Cancello (2009), original in English; no measurement data.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other species of the genus by the combination of small compound eyes and small fontanelle; the most similar species is O. mirim, from which it differs in the labral setae not arranged in rows. The soldier has stout mandibles and a head capsule smaller than in O. heberi, O. insignis, O. orthognathus, O. gibberorum and O. uncimandibularis, with parallel sides of the head in dorsal view (slightly convergent anteriorly in O. brevipilosus and O. longilamina); the most similar species is O. orthognathus, whose soldier is larger.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes small, separated from the lower margin of the head by a distance equal to the greatest diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli kidney-shaped and narrow in dorsal view; oval in lateral view, separated from the compound eye by its least diameter. Fontanelle narrow and small. Head capsule with short hairs and scattered setae. Labral setae not arranged in rows. Pronotum covered with short hairs and setae on the margins; mesonotum and metanotum with short hairs, concentrated on the centre and the posterior margin. Head, pronotum and tergites brown to dark brown, sternites and legs pale brown, wing scales dark brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle slightly prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 2, with a tooth-like process on the proximal half. Head capsule with scattered short hairs and setae, denser ventrally, minute hairs scattered over the whole head capsule and denser in the apical region. Postmentum with short hairs and setae. Pronotum with short hairs and setae, more numerous on the margins; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with setae and short hairs; abdominal tergites and sternites densely setose, the posterior margin of the sternites with erect setae.
